questions.stem:
Assertion: Statins lower the rate of cholesterol synthesis.
Reason: Statins are structural analogues of HMG-CoA that competitively inhibit HMG-CoA reductase, the rate-limiting enzyme.
questions.why: The reason is the exact mechanism of the assertion.

questions.stem:
Assertion: Only palmitate is released by the fatty acid synthase complex.
Reason: The thioesterase of the complex releases the chain once it reaches 16 carbons.
questions.why: Longer chains then need the elongation system.

questions.stem:
Assertion: Essential fatty acids must be supplied in the diet.
Reason: Mammals lack the enzymes to introduce double bonds beyond carbon 9.
questions.why: Hence linoleate and linolenate are essential.

questions.stem:
Assertion: Malonyl-CoA inhibits the oxidation of fatty acids.
Reason: Malonyl-CoA inhibits carnitine acyltransferase I, blocking entry of acyl-CoA into mitochondria.
questions.why: This prevents simultaneous synthesis and oxidation.

questions.stem:
Assertion: Acetyl-CoA carboxylase is the rate-limiting enzyme of fatty-acid synthesis.
Reason: Fatty acid synthase is a single multienzyme complex.
questions.why: Both statements are true, but the multienzyme nature of synthase does not explain why carboxylase is rate-limiting.

questions.stem:
Assertion: β-oxidation takes place in the mitochondrial matrix.
Reason: β-oxidation uses NADPH as its reducing agent.
questions.why: β-oxidation uses FAD and NAD⁺, not NADPH, so the reason is false.

questions.stem:
Assertion: Fatty-acid synthesis uses FADH₂ as its reducing agent.
Reason: NADPH is a more powerful reducing agent than FADH₂.
questions.why: Synthesis uses NADPH, not FADH₂, so the assertion is false.

questions.stem:
Assertion: Cholesterol can be synthesised only in the intestine.
Reason: HMG-CoA reductase is absent from the liver.
questions.why: The liver is a major site of cholesterol synthesis and is rich in the reductase.

questions.stem:
Assertion: A rise in cellular sterol level speeds the degradation of HMG-CoA reductase.
Reason: Cholesterol induces polyubiquitination of the enzyme through its sterol-sensing domain.
questions.why: This is proteolytic feedback control.

questions.stem:
Assertion: Bile-acid synthesis is the main route for eliminating excess cholesterol.
Reason: Bile acids emulsify dietary fat in the intestine.
questions.why: Both are true, but emulsifying fat is a separate function and does not explain cholesterol elimination.

questions.stem:
Assertion: Glycine is not optically active.
Reason: Its side chain is a hydrogen, so its α-carbon is not chiral.
questions.why: A chiral centre needs four different groups.

questions.stem:
Assertion: Serum AST and ALT rise in liver injury.
Reason: They are aminotransferases present in hepatocytes and released when the cells are damaged.
questions.why: They are used as liver biomarkers.

questions.stem:
Assertion: Proline cannot undergo PLP-dependent reactions such as transamination.
Reason: Proline has a secondary amino group.
questions.why: The secondary amino group prevents the usual PLP chemistry.

questions.stem:
Assertion: Lysine and threonine are not transaminated.
Reason: They lack an α-amino group.
questions.why: Both do have α-amino groups; the exception is a feature of their metabolism, so the reason is false.

questions.stem:
Assertion: Tyrosine becomes a dietary essential amino acid in phenylketonuria.
Reason: A deficiency of phenylalanine hydroxylase blocks the conversion of phenylalanine to tyrosine.
questions.why: Tyrosine can then no longer be made.

questions.stem:
Assertion: Transdeamination allows virtually all amino acids to be deaminated.
Reason: It couples transamination with the oxidative deamination of glutamate.
questions.why: Amino groups are funnelled to glutamate, then released.

questions.stem:
Assertion: Proteins are built from D-α-amino acids.
Reason: Only L-α-amino acids are incorporated during protein synthesis.
questions.why: The assertion is false; the reason is the correct fact.

questions.stem:
Assertion: The α-helix is stabilised by hydrogen bonds.
Reason: The bonds form between the atoms of peptide bonds lying above and below along the spiral.
questions.why: This is secondary-structure stabilisation.

questions.stem:
Assertion: The hydroxyl radical is the most reactive oxygen species.
Reason: It reacts strongly with carbohydrates, lipids and proteins.
questions.why: Its high reactivity makes it the most damaging.

questions.stem:
Assertion: Hydrogen peroxide is a reactive oxygen species.
Reason: It contains an unpaired electron.
questions.why: H₂O₂ has no unpaired electron; it is a non-radical ROS, so the reason is false.

questions.stem:
Assertion: Humans depend on dietary vitamin C.
Reason: Humans lack the enzyme L-gulonolactone oxidase.
questions.why: So ascorbate cannot be synthesised.

questions.stem:
Assertion: Peroxynitrite readily oxidises LDL.
Reason: Nitric oxide and superoxide combine to form peroxynitrite.
questions.why: Both are true, but how peroxynitrite is formed does not explain its oxidising action on LDL.

questions.stem:
Assertion: In most diseases oxidative stress is a consequence rather than the cause.
Reason: Increased reactive-species formation accompanies tissue injury.
questions.why: Injury drives the oxidative stress that follows.

questions.stem:
Assertion: Superoxide dismutase converts oxygen directly into water.
Reason: Catalase generates superoxide from hydrogen peroxide.
questions.why: SOD makes hydrogen peroxide from superoxide, and catalase removes hydrogen peroxide; both statements are false.

questions.why: Longer fatty acids come from the elongation system.

questions.stem: True or false: All reactive oxygen species are free radicals.
questions.why: Hydrogen peroxide is a ROS but has no unpaired electron.

questions.stem: True or false: Glycine is optically active.
questions.why: Its side chain is a hydrogen, so it has no chiral centre.

questions.stem: True or false: Essential fatty acids and essential amino acids can both be synthesised by humans.
questions.why: By definition, essential nutrients cannot be made and must be eaten.

questions.stem: True or false: Glutamate dehydrogenase is inhibited by GTP and ATP.
questions.why: GDP and ADP are its activators.

questions.stem: True or false: The hydroxyl radical can be generated by the Fenton reaction.
questions.why: Fe²⁺ reacts with hydrogen peroxide to form it.

questions.stem: True or false: Lysine and threonine readily undergo transamination.
questions.why: They are the two amino acids generally not transaminated.
